source.title: Thinking in Frames: How Visual Context and Test-Time Scaling Empower Video Reasoning
source.authors: Chengzu Li; Zanyi Wang; Jiaang Li; Yi Xu; Han Zhou; Huanyu Zhang; Ruichuan An; Dengyang Jiang; Zhaochong An; Ivan Vulić; Serge Belongie; Anna Korhonen

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports visual inference-frame scaling for video-based planning and compares it by analogy with LLM test-time scaling. It does not test pretraining-loss power laws, their extrapolation, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper's visual test-time scaling results are related to scaling but measure planning performance as video frame budget changes, not the loss or behaviors named by V1–V7. Included as findings under fits_no_version; cited scaling-law results from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study varies inference-time video frame budget (and frames per step κ) for a single fine-tuned 5B video model and reports maze/tangram planning accuracy. It never varies parameters, training tokens or training compute, never measures held-out pretraining loss, and fits no power law. Its 'visual test-time scaling law' is an analogy to LLM test-time compute, not a test of any version V1–V7. It does not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that video generation models can act as visual reasoners that generalize zero-shot. Visual context (icons, tangram piece shapes) works as control. More generated frames act as a test-time reasoning budget that improves OOD long-horizon maze planning within positional-embedding limits. This does not carry over to tangram planning, where maintaining geometric consistency is the bottleneck.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies inference-time video frame budgets for visual planning, not the original training-loss scaling-law measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance depends on task and frame budget: maze performance improves up to 121 frames and declines at 141 for temporal OOD cases; the tangram Translation setting shows no significant gain from more frames. The maze experiments also vary scaling factor κ.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing inference frame count for a fine-tuned Wan 2.2 5B video model improves OOD maze EM/PR from 61 to 121 frames. Temporal-OOD performance drops at 141 frames but stays above the 81-frame baseline. Raising frames per step κ from 5 to 9 helps, with a temporal-OOD drop at κ=11. Tangram Translation shows no significant gain from more frames.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time frame budget in video generation models acts like test-time compute for sequential visual planning, within positional-embedding length limits and depending on the task.

record.problems: The relevant frame-scaling results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text; uncertainty estimates are not stated. The study concerns visual planning performance, not language-model pretraining loss scaling.
record.rows_left_out: No results on language-model held-out loss scaling or related versions were reported. Other visual test-time scaling conditions, including κ sweeps and tangram settings beyond the Translation result, are not separately itemized because the paper's reported descriptions do not provide additional claim-relevant numerical outcomes.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute; no loss is measured.
Extrapolation of fitted power laws from small to large runs.
Architecture shape effects at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss in video or other regimes; the video model's training scale is not varied.
Downstream performance versus model scale or pretraining loss. Models of different sizes are compared (5B vs 20B), but differ in modality and method, so this is not a scaling test.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal split on setup choices.

missing.what: κ (frames-per-step) sweep results: gains from κ=5 to 7/9/11, temporal-OOD peak at κ=9 then decline at κ=11. Only relevant to the fits_no_version finding, not to any version.

record.verdict_notes: The paper uses the phrase 'scaling law' only for inference-time frame budget. No pretraining-loss or training-scale results appear, so the study is T6 for the scaling_laws claim and gets no verdicts. All frame-scaling values are figure-only, with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameter count, tokens, or training compute.
Extrapolating pretraining-loss power-law fits from small to much larger training runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation at fixed training compute.
Effects of architecture shape at fixed parameter count on pretraining loss.
Whether the same power-law form for held-out loss holds in other modalities or training regimes.
Predictability of downstream task performance from model scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of loss-law exponents and compute-optimal allocation on fitting/setup choices, or bending of loss curves.
